title: Twenty-Ninth Post-Cabinet Press Briefing 2026
primaryAgendaItem: Implementation of business licensing reforms and e-hailing review; priority projects; Lake Kariba disaster response; 2026/27 rainfall outlook
summary: Cabinet reviewed implementation of approved licences, permits, levies and fees and approved transitional measures for e-hailing services; adopted the mid-cycle report for the second 100-day cycle; approved immediate measures for communities affected by the Lake Kariba ferry disaster; received the 2026/27 rainfall outlook indicating elevated El Nino-related dryness risk; reviewed the Zimbabwe Agricultural Show and Sanganai/Hlanganani preparations; and received regional and international engagement reports.

highlights.detail: 291 approved reforms have been fully implemented. Local Government has implemented 62 of 201 approved fees through SI 41 and SI 107 of 2026, including removal of Livestock Movement Clearance fees, Fuel Storage Registration Certificate, Cattle levy and Fish Monger licences.

Cabinet approved interim transitional measures including a five-month moratorium while the sector is reviewed, development of a self-regulating framework, ZIMRA registration/tax registration, and development of e-hailing regulations by the Ministry of Transport and Infrastructural Development.
As at day 50 (13 July 2026), 191 of 203 approved priority projects were being implemented; funding for the remaining 12 was at advanced mobilisation stages; 21 projects were set for commissioning.

Immediate measures cover humanitarian relief and psychosocial support, recovery and resilience, transport and infrastructure, and disaster-risk-reduction training, including road repairs, vessel replacement, affordable ferry services, weather stations, drones, communications, water safety and first aid.

A very strong El Nino is expected to increase the likelihood of below-to-normal rainfall. October-December 2026 is expected to trend below-to-normal; January-March 2027 is expected to remain dry/erratic with frequent dry spells and warmer-than-normal temperatures. Government called for contingency planning, water harvesting and conservation.

The 116th Show (24-29 August 2026) recorded estimated attendance of 208,000 versus 198,182 in 2025; 89,000 square metres of space uptake; 600 agri-produce entries; 249 tobacco entries (+105%); 50 cotton entries; 640 commercial exhibitors; and 13 international exhibitors from 9 countries.
Livestock entries increased in beef by 41%, goats 33.9%, sheep 13.39%, pigs 7.14%, rabbits 13.39%, and poultry 146.43%.
Expo scheduled for 9-12 September 2026 at Gymkhana Events and Conference Centre in Masvingo. 385 companies from 15 countries and 153 buyers (125 international, 28 local) had confirmed participation.

Zimbabwe and Mozambique highlighted the Beira-Feruka pipeline expansion project's importance for regional energy security, economic growth and jobs. Angola also indicated readiness to discuss investment/cooperation on the Lobito Refinery Project.
The 21st Extraordinary AU Summit adopted a decision on strengthening conflict-prevention and resolution mechanisms and the Luanda Action Plan with an implementation matrix.

Outcomes included a multilateral Joint Declaration and proposed bilateral broadcasting/online audio-visual cooperation, including joint content production, AI-enabled media technology and talent development.

Zimbabwe was accorded chairmanship of the African Group of Negotiators for a two-year mandate and confirmed as 2027 host of the FAO Committee on Forestry Working Group on Dryland Forests; the Ulaanbaatar Declaration was endorsed.
